issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'לְעֶבֶד מֶלֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁי' means 'to Ebed-melech the Cushite' (Ebed-melech is a proper name, 'servant of the king'). The Chinese renders it as '古實人以伯米勒的僕人' which means 'the servant of Ebed-melech the Cushite', reversing the construct relationship. In Hebrew, 'עֶבֶד מֶלֶךְ' is a proper name (Ebed-melech), not 'servant of the king' as a title. The Chinese adds '的僕人' (the servant of), making it appear that the message is to a servant of Ebed-melech, whereas the Hebrew addresses Ebed-melech himself.
